title: Implement reusable definition update and rename
description: Add provider update behavior for reusable definitions after catalog create/read support exists. Accept partial name, title, and instructions changes with at least one field supplied; preserve ID and createdAt, advance updatedAt monotonically, and atomically replace the validated catalog. A rename must keep every task reference valid because tasks store UUIDs. Enforce case-insensitive name uniqueness while allowing casing-only edits to the same definition. Return unchanged results consistently when supplied values normalize to stored values. Add focused tests for rename stability, partial edits, casing-only updates, no-op handling, duplicate-name rejection, timestamp behavior, and injected atomic-write failure. Do not implement deletion or task detachment here.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Scope confirmed: implement only ReusableTaskMutationProvider.UpdateReusableTask in the existing flat-file provider. Create/list/get already use the global lock, strict catalog validation, and atomic byte replacement; update will preserve UUID/CreatedAt, trim and validate supplied fields, permit same-definition casing edits, return the current definition for normalized no-ops without rewriting, and leave task UUID references untouched. I will add focused provider tests for partial/casing/no-op/duplicate/timestamp/atomic-failure behavior, with no deletion or detachment.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Implemented UpdateReusableTask in internal/provider/flatfile/reusable.go. It resolves by UUID then case-insensitive trimmed name under the global lock, applies partial trimmed name/title/instructions edits, rejects empty patches and invalid/duplicate resulting catalogs, preserves ID/CreatedAt, advances UpdatedAt with the existing monotonic catalog clock, and atomically publishes validated bytes. Normalized no-ops return the stored definition without rewriting; casing-only edits update the stored casing; UUID references remain resolvable after rename. Added focused tests covering rename/reference stability, partial and casing edits, no-op bytes/timestamps, duplicate and empty rejection, future-clock monotonicity, and injected replacement failure with unchanged bytes. No deletion or detachment was added.
